column10: My husband and I are both closer to 50 than 40. We call this stuff WITCHERY, because there?ôs some dark magic at work here in that it DOES in fact work to tighten the skin under the eyes. I insert my contacts first, since you don?ôt want to be tugging at the skin around your eyes after you?ôve applied this magic stuff. I squeeze a TINY amount onto the back of my hand (just slightly more than a grain of rice, but less than the size of a pearl). I use a clean concealer brush that I use only for applying this gel. I dab the end of the brush into the gel and apply under my eyes in small overlapping sections--don?ôt overlap in any one place too much or you?ôll apply too much and end up with the white residue. Then I do the same on the other eye with another rice-to-pear-sized bit of gel squeezed first onto the back of my hand, then applied with a brush. I immediately rinse and clean off the brush in water. Then, without squinting or stretching my face, I apply some serum to my face (avoiding the eye area, like I would do anyway). I apply some moisturizer (again, avoiding the eyes). I do my other post-shower routine--body lotion, deodorant, get dressed. The gel is usually dry within 5 minutes, and you can feel it tightening a bit under your eyes. By the time I?ôm ready to apply makeup, it?ôs dried. I use a primer with SPF and am very gentle with the area under my eyes. I then dab liquid concealer on--including under my eyes. I blend the concealer in gently with my finger (not a brush). Once that has dried, I apply a powder foundation. The makeup routine is essentially the same as always. I just go gently around the eyes. Voila! WITCHERY!
